surfaces.notes: Human output is normalized semantically; JSON output stays schema-exact.
Covers local paths, registry refs, and official skill resolution.
Covers graph execution, branching, caller handoffs, receipts, and the deterministic decision kernel.
Receipt JSON and signature metadata are schema-exact parity surfaces.
Append-only run state and continuation history must survive cutover.
Declared and enforced sandbox metadata must remain distinct.
Harness replay mode proves deterministic fixture execution and sealed receipt checks.
Search/filter behavior is command-level parity with normalized output.
Local and hosted registry envelopes are exercised through native registry commands.
Catalog discovery, dispatch, and local tool builds use the canonical native or manifest-owned path.
Protocol behavior uses local servers and deterministic clients.
Process invocation, env, cwd, and sandbox metadata are parity-critical.
MCP transport and tool results use local protocol fixtures.
Managed agent calls are represented by local stubs, not live providers.
RUNX_HOME, encrypted local profiles, and config file behavior are part of CLI parity.
Public API identity and HTTP transport are resolved once and exercised against deterministic local servers.
The native CLI owns provider-neutral grant lifecycle; governed skills and native provider tools own bounded provider operations.
Diagnostics can add ids, but the documented command surface must not disappear.
Offline data-store migration is bounded, backup-first, idempotent, and independently read back.
Development lanes run deterministic or recorded harness fixtures.
Host-agent shims are generated from validated skill packages and delegate back to governed runx skill execution.
Native parser evaluation output stays schema-exact.
Grant, scope, and authority-kind policy remains machine-checkable without OSS brokerage.
Policy inspection and linting stay machine-checkable before mutation gates run.
Required input, approvals, and agent work keep the same continuation contract.
Skill creation uses one digest-bound inspect, plan, bind, validate, harness, and transactional apply lane.
Deterministic project and global workspace initialization remains separate from skill authoring.
Prefetch and lockfile behavior stays fixture-backed.
Inventory output for tools, skills, graphs, packets, and overlays stays represented.
External process extension output and manifest validation remain schema-exact.
